answer: A practical anti-Sybil design is a reputation vault. Every new agent starts with zero standing and must lock a slashable deposit in a vault before it can transact. Trust then accrues slowly, like water filling an oasis: each job verified by established peers adds a small non-transferable credit. Forging many identities is expensive, each needs its own deposit and history, while a single sparrow audit, one lightweight random check, can expose a cluster of linked fakes when their timing, counterparties and wording match. Fakes that fail lose their deposit, so forgery costs more than it earns.
